original_problem.title: A
original_problem.description:
You have an array a with length n, you can perform operations. Each operation is like this: choose two adjacent elements from a, say x and y, and replace one of them with gcd(x, y), where gcd denotes the greatest common divisor.

What is the minimum number of operations you need to make all of the elements equal to 1?


-----Input-----

The first line of the input contains one integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2000) — the number of elements in the array.

The second line contains n space separated integers a_1, a_2, ..., a_{n} (1 ≤ a_{i} ≤ 10^9) — the elements of the array.


-----Output-----

Print -1, if it is impossible to turn all numbers to 1. Otherwise, print the minimum number of operations needed to make all numbers equal to 1.


-----Examples-----
Input
5
2 2 3 4 6

Output
5

Input
4
2 4 6 8

Output
-1

Input
3
2 6 9

Output
4



-----Note-----

In the first sample you can turn all numbers to 1 using the following 5 moves:

  [2, 2, 3, 4, 6].  [2, 1, 3, 4, 6]  [2, 1, 3, 1, 6]  [2, 1, 1, 1, 6]  [1, 1, 1, 1, 6]  [1, 1, 1, 1, 1] 

We can prove that in this case it is not possible to make all numbers one using less than 5 moves.
original_problem.output:

We can prove that in this case it is not possible to make all numbers one using less than 5 moves.

difference_plan.rationale: The rule mandates changes to objective, core constraints, and invariants to support a counting formulation. Input structure is only lightly themed but otherwise unaltered.
difference_plan.summary: Objective shifted from minimize to count_with_mod; core constraints added counting definitions, modulus, and phase decomposition; invariants restructured to support counting of optimal sequences via subarray generation and spread phases.

components.role_description: list of skill levels of students, representing their current competency

constraints.name: allowed_operation
constraints.description: Each operation chooses two adjacent students and replaces the skill level of one of them with the greatest common divisor of their current skill levels. Formally, for adjacent positions i,i+1, replace skills[i] or skills[i+1] with gcd(skills[i], skills[i+1]).
constraints.formal: ∀ operation: pick adjacent x,y; replace one with gcd(x,y)

constraints.name: target_state_all_ones
constraints.description: The goal is to make the skill level of all students equal to 1. If it is impossible, return -1; otherwise, return the number of optimal operation sequences (those with the minimum possible number of operations) modulo MOD.
constraints.formal: final state: skills[i]=1 for all i; if impossible output -1 else output count mod MOD

constraints.name: optimal_sequence_definition
constraints.description: An operation sequence is a finite ordered list of operations. Two sequences are distinct if at some step t the chosen adjacent pair or the student replaced differs. An optimal sequence is one that uses the minimum number of operations to achieve all ones.
constraints.formal: distinct if ∃ t: different (pos, replacement_side); optimal if length = minimum_possible

constraints.name: counting_modulus
constraints.description: The answer (the number of optimal sequences) must be taken modulo MOD = 1,000,000,007.

constraints.name: phase_decomposition
constraints.description: In any optimal sequence, operations naturally split into two non-overlapping phases: (1) generating the first 1 in a contiguous subarray whose overall gcd is 1, using exactly len-1 operations; (2) spreading the 1 to all remaining non-1 elements, using n-1 operations. The two phases are independent in counting.
constraints.formal: phase1 = create first 1 in some interval [l,r] with gcd=1 and len = r-l+1 minimal; phase1 operations = len-1; phase2 = spread from first 1 position to all other n-1 positions, operations = n-1; phases disjoint in optimal case

constraints.name: impossibility_condition
constraints.description: If the gcd of the entire initial array is not 1, then no sequence exists.

objective.description: Output the number of distinct optimal operation sequences modulo 1,000,000,007. If it is impossible, output -1.

invariants.name: global_gcd_invariance
invariants.description: The gcd of the entire array is invariant under operations, so feasibility is equivalent to initial global gcd being 1.

invariants.name: optimal_structure_lowerbound
invariants.description: The minimum number of operations is determined by the shortest subarray with gcd=1. If such a subarray exists of length L, then min_ops = (L-1) + (n-1).

invariants.name: generation_phase_counting_unit
invariants.description: For a given interval of length L achieving gcd=1, the number of distinct operation sequences of length L-1 that result in at least one 1 inside the interval can be computed via dp on interval merging. The set of such sequences is the primary counting unit.

invariants.name: spread_phase_counting_unit
invariants.description: Once a 1 exists at position p, the number of sequences of n-1 operations spreading it to all positions is equal to C(n-1, p-1) (binomial coefficient), independent of the generation phase.

invariants.name: non_overlap_guarantee
invariants.description: In any optimal sequence, no operation that affects a 1 can be used to help generate the first 1, so phases are strictly sequential and non-interfering, allowing product counting.

generated_problem.title: 技能达标最优方案数
generated_problem.description:
校园编程社最近发起了一项全员达标活动：让每位成员的技能等级都变为 1，即入门水平。社长林小树想出了一种结对互助的方法，并制定了操作规则。

社团有 n 名成员排成一排，第 i 名成员的初始技能等级为 s_i。每次操作，你可以选择相邻的两名成员，计算他们当前技能等级的最大公约数（gcd），然后指定其中一人的技能等级直接变成这个公约数。注意，替换哪一名由你决定，每一次操作都会改变队列的状态。

目标是使所有成员的技能等级都变为 1。若初始无法达成（即所有 s_i 的 gcd 不为 1），输出 -1。否则，你需要求出在**使用最少操作次数**达成目标的前提下，一共有多少种不同的操作序列？

两条操作序列不同，当且仅当在某个步骤，你选择的相邻位置不同，或者虽然位置相同但你替换的成员不同。

可以证明，所有最优操作序列都可以唯一地分解为两个阶段：
- 生成阶段：选定一个长度最小的连续子数组，其元素的 gcd 为 1，通过恰好 len−1 次操作在该子数组内产生至少一个 1；
- 传播阶段：通过恰好 n−1 次操作，将已产生的 1 依次传播到其余所有位置。

不同最小子数组可能对应不同的生成方案，传播阶段的方案数由第一个 1 产生的位置决定。在统计总数时，需将每个可能的最小生成子数组对应的方案数相加，但要注意避免因子数组重叠而重复计数。（上述分解为自然结论，可直接使用。）

最终答案对 1,000,000,007 取模。
generated_problem.input_format:
第一行包含一个整数 n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2000)，表示成员的数量。
第二行包含 n 个空格分隔的整数 s_1, s_2, ..., s_n (1 ≤ s_i ≤ 10^9)，依次表示成员的初始技能等级。
generated_problem.output_format: 输出一个整数。如果无法使所有技能等级变为 1，输出 -1；否则输出方案数对 1,000,000,007 取模的结果。

samples.explanation: 数组共有两个最短子数组 [2,3] 和 [3,4] 可使 gcd 为 1，最少操作次数为 (2-1)+(5-1)=5。对于每个子数组，生成阶段有 2 种方案产生第一个 1，传播阶段方案数分别为 C(4,1)=4 和 C(4,2)=6（依第一个 1 的位置而定）。两个子数组无重叠方案，总计 2×(4+6)=20。
所有技能等级的 gcd 为 2，不可能产生 1。
整个数组 gcd 为 1，最短子数组长度为 3，最少操作数为 (3-1)+(3-1)=4。生成阶段有 3 种方案，传播阶段的方案组合后总数为 3。
已经达标，空操作序列是唯一的最优序列。

generated_problem.notes: 本题中方案数可能很大，请务必对 1,000,000,007 取模后输出。统计时需确保每条最优操作序列被计数恰好一次，尤其当存在多个最短子数组时要注意它们的重叠关系，避免重复计数。

algorithmic_delta_claim.seed_solver_core: Scan for existing 1s, find the shortest contiguous subarray with gcd=1, compute min_ops = (len-1) + (n-1).
algorithmic_delta_claim.reusable_subroutines: Prefix/suffix gcd computation and sliding window to locate shortest gcd-1 subarray remain reusable for determining optimality and phase separation.
algorithmic_delta_claim.new_solver_core: For each shortest subarray achieving gcd=1, run an interval DP to count distinct sequences of length len-1 that produce a 1 (considering different merge orders). Multiply by the number of spreading sequences from the resulting 1 position using binomial coefficients. Sum over all shortest subarrays (with possible overlap handling to avoid double-counting). Modulo arithmetic on all combinations.
algorithmic_delta_claim.new_proof_obligation: Prove that the generation-phase counting DP correctly enumerates all distinct operation sequences without double-counting or omission. Prove independence of phases under the optimality condition and that the product formula is valid. Verify that handling multiple disjoint or overlapping shortest intervals yields correct total count, including when an initial 1 already exists.
algorithmic_delta_claim.why_direct_reuse_fails: The original solver only extracts a minimum number; it has no mechanism to enumerate or combine different operation orders. Counting requires combinatorial logic (interval DP, binomial coefficients) and careful handling of equivalences that were irrelevant for the minimization version.

review_context.anti_shallow_rationale: The transformation goes far beyond retheming: it changes the mathematical question from existence/minimum to counting, introduces new structural constraints (phase decomposition, deduplication rules), and demands a fundamentally different solver with combinatorial DP and modular arithmetic. The campus theme is only a narrative wrapper.
